hints: Specify a minimum energy and an electron at the metal surface.
walkthrough: the minimum energy required to release an electron from the surface of a metal

hints: Find photon energy from wavelength, then subtract the work function.
The remaining energy is the maximum kinetic energy of an electron.
The maximum applies to electrons escaping without extra energy losses inside the metal.
walkthrough: Most emitted electrons require energy to reach the surface from within the metal, leaving less kinetic energy and hence a speed below the maximum.

hints: Separate energy per photon from the number of photons arriving per second.
At fixed intensity, increasing photon energy reduces the photon arrival rate.
walkthrough: Reduced intensity at constant frequency: energy per photon is unchanged, so maximum electron speed has no change; fewer photons arrive per second, so the emission rate decreases.

Increased frequency at constant intensity: photon energy increases, giving a higher maximum electron speed. The same incident power is carried by fewer photons per second, so the emission rate decreases.
Table entries in row order: no change; decreases; increases; decreases.
